description: Each station's average bandwidth usage is compared against the mean bandwidth usage over all individual telescopes.

c.request: Which observatory stations (`observstation`) have an average telescope bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) above the overall average bandwidth usage? Ignore missing values. For each one, show the station, its average bandwidth usage, and how much it exceeds the overall average. Return the top 10 by that margin, largest first, without rounding. Each station's average bandwidth usage is compared against the mean bandwidth usage over all individual telescopes.
c.sql: SELECT t.observstation, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusagepct, AVG(t.bandusagepct) - (SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) FROM telescopes WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL) AS above_overall_avg FROM telescopes AS t WHERE t.bandusagepct IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.observstation HAVING AVG(t.bandusagepct) > (SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) FROM telescopes WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY above_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each observatory station, calculate the average non-missing bandwidth usage of its telescopes and compare it with the average non-missing bandwidth usage across all individual telescopes; return the 10 stations with the largest positive differences, showing the station, its average, and the difference, in descending order without rounding
b.sql:
WITH overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) AS overall_avg
  FROM telescopes
), station_avgs AS (
  SELECT observstation, AVG(bandusagepct) AS station_avg
  FROM telescopes
  GROUP BY observstation
)
SELECT
  s.observstation,
  s.station_avg,
  s.station_avg - o.overall_avg AS difference
FROM station_avgs AS s
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE s.station_avg > o.overall_avg
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 10;

a.request: For each observatory station (`observstation`), compute the average bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) of its telescopes, ignoring missing values. Compute the overall average across all individual telescopes, so stations with more telescopes weigh more. Keep only the stations whose average is above this overall average. Show the station, its average bandwidth usage, and how far it is above the overall average (station average minus overall average). Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return the top 10, without rounding.
a.sql:
WITH station_averages AS (
  SELECT
    observstation,
    AVG(bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusagepct
  FROM telescopes
  GROUP BY observstation
), overall_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusagepct
  FROM telescopes
)
SELECT
  s.observstation,
  s.avg_bandusagepct,
  s.avg_bandusagepct - o.avg_bandusagepct AS above_overall_average
FROM station_averages AS s
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o
WHERE s.avg_bandusagepct > o.avg_bandusagepct
ORDER BY above_overall_average DESC
LIMIT 10;

d.request: Which observatory stations (`observstation`) have an average telescope bandwidth usage (`bandusagepct`) above the mean bandwidth usage across all individual telescopes? Ignore missing values. For each station, show its average bandwidth usage and its margin above that overall mean. Return the top 10 stations by margin, largest first, without rounding.
d.sql: SELECT t.observstation, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusagepct, AVG(t.bandusagepct) - (SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) FROM telescopes WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL) AS margin_above_mean FROM telescopes AS t WHERE t.bandusagepct IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.observstation HAVING AVG(t.bandusagepct) > (SELECT AVG(bandusagepct) FROM telescopes WHERE bandusagepct IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY margin_above_mean DESC LIMIT 10;
